summary: The Verge's 2023 holiday gift guide for kids, written by Antonio G. Di Benedetto, lists about 30 gift ideas with short blurbs, prices, and retailers. The picks span games, toys, tech gadgets, clothing, books and creative tools, from Poetry for Neanderthals and Magna-Tiles to the Kindle Kids, iPad and Nintendo Switch Lite. A few items are aimed at older kids, such as the Pinecil soldering iron.
one_line: The Verge's 2023 kids gift guide recommends roughly 30 games, toys, gadgets and accessories with prices and retailers, from $8.95 to $249+.
key_facts: Poetry for Neanderthals is a party game for up to six players who must get teammates to guess a word using only single-syllable words, and it costs $19.99.
Disney Illusion Island for Nintendo Switch is a 2D "Metroidvania"-style game with co-op for up to four players, where you can hug a struggling player to restore health; price $39.88+.
The Magna-Tiles Jungle Animals set has 25 pieces, includes a caiman and a magnetic sloth, and costs $39.99.
The Kindle Kids (2022) has a 6.2-inch display, USB-C charging, weeks of battery life, no ads and a two-year accident warranty, priced at $119.99.
The Nintendo Switch Lite (Isabelle's Aloha Edition) has a 5.5-inch display, an Animal Crossing-inspired design and a digital copy of New Horizons, for $199.99.
The Apple iPad (2021), ninth-gen, has a 10.2-inch screen, a 12MP camera and a 3.5mm headphone jack, and costs $249+.
The Kit Adam by KBDcraft is a hot-swappable 60 percent mechanical keyboard with a Lego-style brick case, priced at $99.99.
The BuddyPhones Cosmos Plus are noise-canceling, wireless and wired kids' headphones with a volume limiter, priced at $79.90+.
The Echo Dot Kids (fifth-gen) costs $27.99 and comes with a one-year Amazon Kids Plus subscription and a two-year accident protection plan.
The new Furby is a voice-activated animatronic plushie that works fully offline with no "smart" functionality, priced at $49.
The Nerf Perses MXIX-5000 motorized blaster shoots soft foam balls at up to eight per second and costs $59.99+.
The Original Bazooka Bubble Gun is battery-powered, fires over 5,000 bubbles per minute, and costs $32.39.
The Pinecil portable soldering iron is meant only for responsible teens or early teens, can run off a USB-C PD power bank, and costs $25.99+.
The Mark-my-time digital bookmark has a built-in timer for tracking reading sessions and costs $8.95+.
